title: Demonstration against COVID-19 restrictions on Amsterdam Museumplein
organizer: Nederland in Verzet (identified by Euronews; organizers cancelled the official event after rejecting the assigned site and cap)
participants_original: NL Times: “well over a thousand”; Euronews and DutchNews: officials estimated about 2,000.
threshold_50_evidence: A local report says well over a thousand people appeared; two reports attribute an estimate of about 2,000 to officials. This establishes the 50-person threshold, while exact bounds remain unknown.

start_date.summary: All three opened contemporary reports identify the gathering as Sunday 17 January 2021.

location.summary: Reports place the gathering at Museumplein in Amsterdam.

demands.summary: Reports describe opposition to government COVID restrictions and possible curfew, with anti-lockdown placards.

organizer.summary: Euronews names Nederland in Verzet; NL Times says the organizer cancelled after disputing the designated site and 500-person cap.

participants_original.summary: NL Times says well over a thousand showed up; Euronews and DutchNews report an official estimate around 2,000. These are published approximations, not precise bounds.

participants_estimate.summary: Officials estimated about 2,000; retained as approximate.

protester_violence.summary: Reports describe a subset throwing stones, bricks or fireworks at police; violence is coded at event level but limited to a subset.

state_response.arrests.summary: Reports state 143 arrests connected to the demonstration.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Water cannon and mounted riot police were used after warnings and an emergency order to clear Museumplein.

end_date.summary: The square was clear by mid-afternoon/around 17:00, but some people remained on nearby streets; end of the whole gathering is not established.

notes: The organizers cancelled the permitted event, but a large unauthorized public gathering occurred at Museumplein. Keep this separate from the 24 January Museumplein anti-curfew gathering and the later curfew-related criminal episodes unless continuity evidence establishes a link. Protest violence reported by sources concerns a subset; it does not establish the crowd as a whole acted violently.
open_questions: Physical end of participants remaining on streets nearby is unknown.
Compare local reports to determine whether the Amsterdam gathering on 24 January had a distinct organizer, demand articulation and crowd.
Identify additional January gatherings beyond the widely reported Amsterdam demonstrations.

title: Demonstration against government COVID measures at 18 Septemberplein
participants_original: NOS: “hundreds of people” gathered in both Eindhoven and Amsterdam; NOS live blog says hundreds returned to the square after an initial dispersal.
threshold_50_evidence: NOS contemporaneous reporting describes hundreds at this specific public demonstration; that qualitative report establishes a crowd above 50 without a manufactured count.

start_date.summary: Both reports place the demonstration on Sunday 24 January 2021.

location.summary: The demonstration was at 18 Septemberplein in central Eindhoven.

demands.summary: NOS says the demonstrations opposed government COVID measures and coronavirus policy; the evening-curfew context was also present.

participants_original.summary: NOS calls the city crowd “hundreds”; the live blog separately says the first crowd was “tens” and later hundreds returned after dispersal.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: NOS describes hundreds at this site, sufficient qualitative evidence above 50, while exact attendance remains unknown.

organizer.summary: Reports say Nederland in Verzet and Pegida wanted a demonstration and that a “coffee” gathering occurred; who organized the actual Eindhoven crowd remains unclear.

protester_violence.summary: NOS says some demonstrators threw fireworks at police and stones in Eindhoven; NRC quotes ANP that police hit/struck back at demonstrators with batons. The actions are attributed to subsets; no behavior is assigned to the whole crowd.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police used a water cannon, tear gas and other crowd-control methods to clear the banned demonstration; the live report says people were called to leave.

state_response.arrests.summary: NOS live blog reports 30 demonstrators arrested at the first charge, distinct from later totals of 55 arrests connected to disorder.

end_date.summary: Police initially ended the demonstration, but NOS reports hundreds returned to the square after the first dispersal and later disorder continued; physical end of the qualifying assembly is not established.

state_response.beatings.summary: NRC quotes ANP that the ME struck back/warded off demonstrators with batons in Eindhoven. This is direct evidence of baton strikes, not merely a baton-equipped formation; individual victims are not identified.

notes: The 24 January demonstration is distinct from subsequent Eindhoven property damage and looting. Reports distinguish some demonstrators who wanted to oppose COVID measures from later criminal rioters. Violence evidence concerns a subset and needs review. Hundreds returned after an initial dispersal, so the first charge does not establish the physical end. NRC separately provides direct evidence of police baton strikes (ANP wording: the ME struck back/warded off demonstrators with batons); this supports beatings yes, but does not imply every demonstrator was hit.
open_questions: Clarify links among Nederland in Verzet, Pegida and the actual gathering.
Check whether subsequent nighttime disorder included any separate assembly with an explicit state demand.

title: Demonstration against COVID measures on Amsterdam Museumplein
participants_original: NOS: around 250 people at about 14:30, later police estimate about 1,500; 190 arrests.
threshold_50_evidence: The live blog says the municipality treated several banner-holding groups as one demonstration at around 250 people, and NOS later reports the police estimate of about 1,500. Both reported approximations are above 50, not exact counts.

start_date.summary: All three opened NOS reports identify Sunday 24 January 2021.

location.summary: The gathering was on Amsterdam Museumplein; later police operations extended to nearby streets.

demands.summary: NOS describes banners and demonstrators opposing government COVID measures and coronavirus rules.

participants_original.summary: At about 14:30 the municipality counted around 250 persons in banner-holding groups as one demonstration; later police estimated about 1,500.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both directly reported approximate crowd descriptions, around 250 and around 1,500, exceed 50.

organizer.summary: A Nederland in Verzet organizer had announced a coffee gathering after the organized demonstration was cancelled; the city treated groups with banners as one demonstration. Participant and organizer relationships remain uncertain.

protester_violence.summary: NOS reports stones and heavy fireworks thrown at police by demonstrators. This is attributed to some attendees and is not generalized to the entire crowd.

state_response.arrests.summary: NOS reports 190 people arrested in connection with the demonstration.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The municipality ordered the demonstration to end and issued an emergency order; police used sound warnings, water cannon, dogs and horses to clear the square and nearby streets.

end_date.summary: The square was cleared and calm had largely returned by early evening, but the report does not verify the final departure of every participant; physical end remains unresolved.

notes: Keep separate from the 17 January Museumplein gathering: this is a new 24 January anti-COVID-rules assembly, though it may belong to the same campaign. Do not merge solely because venue and organizer overlap. Later criminal rioting is distinct unless evidence shows the same ongoing protest demand.
open_questions: Determine physical end after the gathering moved into nearby streets.
Review whether this and the 17 January event are separate MM events or a linked campaign under the missing additional Coding Procedure.

title: Demonstration against COVID measures at Oude Markt, Enschede
participants_original: NOS live blog: “tientallen” (dozens) gathered; no exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: The source confirms a public demonstration but uses “dozens,” which does not establish that at least 50 gathered.

start_date.summary: NOS live update is dated 24 January 2021.

location.summary: The gathering was at Oude Markt in Enschede.

demands.summary: The report explicitly says attendees demonstrated against COVID measures.

participants_original.summary: NOS uses “tientallen” (dozens); exact attendance is not reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” could be below or above 50; threshold is unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: Fireworks are reported but the source does not say they were directed at the state.

state_response.summary: NOS says police were present and had not intervened at the time of the update; other responses and later developments are unknown.

notes: Retain as a possible policy demonstration. Fireworks and a generally tense atmosphere do not establish violence against the state; no criminal-riot episode is automatically combined with it.
open_questions: Find local reporting or official records to establish the crowd threshold and event end.

title: Announced “Tilburg in opstand” gathering near Wandelboslaan
participants_original: NOS live blog says many people gathered; no numeric estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: A vague “many people” description does not establish at least 50.

location.summary: The report places the crowd near Wandelboslaan in Tilburg-West.

demands.summary: The wording “Tilburg in opstand” is reported and NRC describes an inciting call followed by a municipal emergency order, but neither source identifies a policy demand.

participants_original.summary: The report says “many people,” without a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count; the 50-person threshold remains unverified.

protester_violence.summary: Fireworks and damage to street furniture are reported without attributing them to the whole assembly or showing an anti-state action.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is established in this update.

notes: Unresolved lead only. The wording “Tilburg in opstand” and reports of fireworks/property damage do not alone prove a demand on the Dutch state.
open_questions: Verify whether this was a public protest or curfew-related criminal disorder, what state-policy demand was made, and whether at least 50 people attended.

title: Crowd and unrest near Venlo station
participants_original: NOS live blog: a “large group” was reported; no headcount.
threshold_50_evidence: The phrase “large group” is not numerically precise enough to establish at least 50.

start_date.summary: A NOS live update dated 24 January reports the group near Venlo station that evening.

location.summary: The group was near the railway station in Venlo.

demands.summary: No demand or policy target is identified in the report.

participants_original.summary: NOS says a “large group”; NRC says police were deployed in Venlo after a curfew-related street crowd. No number is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numeric count; threshold remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: The group reportedly threw stones; the report does not establish a protest action or how violence related to any policy demand.

notes: Unresolved lead for follow-up only. The source documents street disorder and stone throwing, not an explicit anti-state protest; do not code the crowd as a qualifying protest unless demand and assembly evidence is found.
open_questions: Find local reports to determine whether this was a public demonstration against the curfew or criminal disorder without a state demand; establish attendance and response.

title: Crowd near Hobbemaplein/Hobbemastraat, Schilderswijk
location: Hobbemaplein and Hobbemastraat, Schilderswijk, The Hague
participants_original: NOS/NRC report a crowd or large group near Hobbemastraat; no number is given.

start_date.summary: A NOS live update dated 24 January describes street activity that evening after a social-media call to demonstrate.

location.summary: A demonstration was called at Hobbemaplein; a fire and crowd were reported on nearby Hobbemastraat.

demands.summary: NRC reports a nearby online call to demonstrate but identifies no demand or policy target.

participants_original.summary: NOS/NRC describe a crowd or large group near Hobbemaplein/Hobbemastraat; no number is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number; threshold cannot be determined.

protester_violence.summary: NRC says heavy fireworks were thrown at bystanders and police; conduct and demand of the full crowd remain uncertain.

notes: Unresolved lead only. A call to demonstrate followed by a crowd and street fire does not by itself establish that the crowd made a demand of government.
open_questions: Establish whether a protest occurred, its state-policy demand, attendance, and relation to separate curfew-night disorder.

title: Demonstration against the curfew in Stein
participants_original: NRC reports approximately 100 youths gathered in protest against curfew; NOS describes dozens of youths. The count and official framing conflict.
threshold_50_evidence: NRC’s contemporary account says approximately 100 youths gathered in protest against the curfew; NOS gives the qualitative count “dozens,” which does not resolve the exact number.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the gathering to Saturday 23 January 2021.

location.summary: The gathering was in Stein, Limburg; exact street location is not established.

demands.summary: NRC describes the gathering as a protest against the nationwide curfew, a government restriction.

participants_original.summary: NRC says approximately 100; NOS says dozens, leaving the exact count unresolved.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: NRC explicitly reports about 100 youths gathered in protest against the curfew, above 50; the NOS qualitative estimate conflicts but is not numerically precise.

protester_violence.summary: NRC reports fireworks thrown at police, supporting yes for violence by a subset; NOS reports fireworks without specifying the target, and the mayor disputed that this was a demonstration. Do not attribute conduct to the whole crowd.

state_response.arrests.summary: Fourteen arrests are reported for the gathering or disorder.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: NRC reports riot police were deployed; whether deployment was an explicit attempt to end the protest needs local-source review.

end_date.summary: NRC reports calm by about 23:00, but not the physical departure of all participants.

notes: NRC reports about 100 youths gathered in protest against the curfew, while NOS describes dozens; the mayor disputed the demonstration label and described deliberate riots. NRC reports fireworks thrown at police; NOS does not specify a target. Code violence at event level based on the attributed subset, not the whole gathering. Fourteen arrests are reported for the gathering or disorder; participant overlap and physical end remain unresolved.
open_questions: Find municipal or police records to resolve the attendance and relationship between protest participants and people involved in criminal disorder.
Clarify whether fireworks were directed at police, other state actors, or unrelated surroundings.
Establish whether riot police or another authority attempted to end the assembly, beyond being called to the area.

title: Demonstration against the curfew near Urk harbor
participants_original: NOS/NRC describe dozens of youths; reports also mention about 100 cars, which are not participant counts.
threshold_50_evidence: A contemporaneous report says dozens of youths gathered to demonstrate against the curfew; no count establishes whether the group exceeded 50. The cars are excluded from attendance.

start_date.summary: Reports date the gathering to the first curfew night, 23 January 2021.

location.summary: Youth gathered around Urk harbor/port; a separate GGD testing site was set on fire nearby.

demands.summary: NRC reports youths went out to protest against the curfew.

participants_original.summary: Reports use “dozens” for youths, while describing around 100 cars; vehicles are not counted as participants.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The attendance description “dozens” does not determine whether 50 people were present.

protester_violence.summary: Reports say some youths threw fireworks and stones at police and damaged police vehicles. The separate test-site fire is not itself evidence of violence against the state.

state_response.arrests.summary: NRC reports two arrests; a retrospective live update says multiple people were detained.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: NRC reports a mayoral emergency order and that the harbor area was cleared around 23:30; verify direct police dispersal orders.

end_date.summary: Area reportedly cleared around 23:30, but exact physical departure of the protesting group is not documented.

notes: Cars, arson and damage do not count as crowd attendance. Do not attribute the GGD-site attack to all attendees or treat property damage alone as protester violence against the state.
open_questions: Confirm the crowd threshold and the extent of state orders/intervention from local official records.
Keep the GGD-site arson separate unless evidence connects it to this gathering and a state demand.

title: Demonstration against coronavirus measures in central Rotterdam
location: Central Rotterdam, including the Markthal area
participants_original: NRC: about 100 people demonstrated against coronavirus measures; RTL: around 50 demonstrators remained outdoors after curfew.
threshold_50_evidence: NRC reports about 100 demonstrators against COVID measures in Rotterdam before curfew. RTL reports around 50 demonstrators remained outside after curfew; these are different phases, not contradictory estimates of one instant.

start_date.summary: Reports identify Saturday 23 January 2021, when the curfew first took effect.

location.summary: The gathering was in central Rotterdam, with reporting mentioning the Markthal area.

demands.summary: NRC describes a demonstration against coronavirus measures; the first-curfew policy was in force.

participants_original.summary: NRC says about 100 people demonstrated against coronavirus measures; RTL says around 50 demonstrators remained outside after curfew.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: NRC reports about 100 people demonstrating before curfew, establishing a crowd above 50; RTL’s around-50 report concerns the later after-curfew phase.

state_response.arrests.summary: RTL reports three protesters arrested; NOS says a few were arrested and several received curfew fines.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: NRC says police broke up the remaining short demonstration after curfew.

end_date.summary: NRC reports police broke up the remaining short demonstration on 23 January; the calendar end date is established, though the exact physical departure time is not reported.

notes: NRC reports about 100 demonstrators before curfew; RTL’s around-50 count is the later group remaining after curfew. Keep these time-specific counts distinct. NRC says police broke up the remaining short demonstration on 23 January; exact departure time is unknown. Fines are not a separate MM response category.
open_questions: Find local Rotterdam reporting and organizer information; confirm whether the estimates refer to the same protest and establish physical end.

title: Anti-fascism demonstration in Amsterdam Westerpark
organizer: Anti-fascist organizers; named organization not established in opened source
participants_original: The municipality estimated about 350 demonstrators; the permitted maximum was 500.
threshold_50_evidence: The municipal estimate reported by NOS was about 350, above the 50-person threshold.

start_date.summary: NOS dates the demonstration to Sunday, 10 January 2021.

end_date.summary: The municipality stated the Westerpark demonstration was over and told participants to maintain spacing while leaving; end date recorded as 10 January, with exact departure time unknown.

location.summary: NOS identifies Westerpark in Amsterdam; organizers’ original planned location differed and the gathering was moved there.

demands.summary: The demonstration opposed fascism after the U.S. Capitol attack; organizers also cited growing far-right sentiment in the Netherlands. A direct demand to Dutch state authorities is not stated, so the demand mapping is provisional and eligibility stays pending.

participants_original.summary: The city estimated about 350 demonstrators and permitted up to 500.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Reported municipal estimate of about 350 exceeds 50.

protester_violence.summary: The city described the event as orderly; the opened account reports no protester violence.

notes: Keep separate from the 17 January Museumplein COVID-measures protest and other January Westerpark notices. The domestic-target requirement is unresolved: antifascism is explicit, but the opened source does not identify a specific demand addressed to the Dutch state. City reporting says it was orderly and that the demonstration had ended; no state-response category can be assigned beyond the documented administrative move/police presence without clearer evidence.
open_questions: Did organizers state a demand for action by the Dutch government or another domestic state authority?
Can an organizer primary statement clarify the target without conflating opposition to fascism with a state demand?
Were any arrests, physical force, or other state responses reported for this gathering?

title: Demonstration against the lockdown and COVID measures in Hilversum
organizer: Nederland in Opstand (reported); speakers included Willem Engel and Tinus Koops
participants_original: RTL/ANP says hundreds. NH Nieuws search-result excerpt estimates approximately 400–500 at the Marktplein.
threshold_50_evidence: RTL/ANP reports hundreds; NH Nieuws local search-result excerpt reports about 400–500 participants.

start_date.summary: Both contemporaneous reports date the protest to 10 January 2021.

end_date.summary: The city called on participants to leave at 15:20 and the square was empty around 16:00.

organizer.summary: NH Nieuws search result names Nederland in Opstand; RTL reports its leader Tinus Koops among speakers.

demands.summary: The gathering opposed the current COVID measures and lockdown; the Dutch policy target is explicit.

participants_original.summary: RTL reports hundreds; NH Nieuws result gives approximately 400–500.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both reports establish hundreds, and NH Nieuws gives approximately 400–500.

protester_violence.summary: The account describes dancing and distancing violations but no violence against the state.

state_response.summary: Municipality ordered participants to leave at 15:20 and the square was empty around 16:00. RTL says one person was arrested for an unspecified reason and no fines were issued; no evidence in these reports of accommodation, beatings, killings or shootings.

notes: The announced Jan. 10 gathering occurred and reached the threshold. Its municipal termination is coded as crowd dispersal because the municipality told participants to leave and the square subsequently emptied. One arrest is reported, but the reason is not linked to protest conduct; arrests is yes at the event level only.
open_questions: What was the reason for the one reported arrest?
Can another local report clarify whether participants left voluntarily after the city order or were physically moved?

title: Demonstration against COVID measures on Amsterdam Museumplein
participants_original: The municipality reported about 200 at 14:31 and later about 600 on the Museumplein.
threshold_50_evidence: The municipality reported about 200 at 14:31 and later about 600 on the square.

start_date.summary: NOS dates the gathering and related city demonstrations to 31 January 2021.

location.summary: Museumplein, with later police action and demonstrators in nearby streets.

demands.summary: NOS explicitly says participants gathered to protest cabinet COVID measures.

participants_original.summary: The city said about 200 were present at 14:31 and about 600 later; counts are time-specific.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both the initial about-200 and later about-600 estimates exceed 50.

protester_violence.summary: The municipality said objects were thrown at police while officers were issuing fines. Violence is recorded for this assembly, but the report does not attribute the act to all participants.

state_response.summary: Police called for the group to leave, then moved people off the square; a water cannon was briefly used in adjacent Van Baerlestraat. Thirty arrests were reported on nearby Valeriusplein, but the report does not establish that detainees were assembly participants, so arrests remains unknown.

notes: The gathering was a demonstration against COVID measures; distinguish it from later street disorder and from 30 arrests on nearby Valeriusplein whose participant status is unverified. The field cleared but participants remained in adjacent streets, so physical end of the wider gathering is unknown. Objects thrown at police are reported during the assembly response and apply to some people, not the whole crowd. Baton-equipped police are reported elsewhere as a line/formation; this is not evidence of baton strikes.
open_questions: When did participants leave the surrounding streets?
Were the 30 people arrested on Valeriusplein participants in this gathering or another public-order group?
Is there direct evidence that batons struck demonstrators?

title: Demonstration against COVID measures at Zwitsalterrein in Apeldoorn
participants_original: NOS reported about 400 demonstrators at Zwitsalterrein.

start_date.summary: NOS dates the demonstration to Sunday, 31 January 2021.

end_date.summary: NOS reports demonstrators left the Zwitsalterrein peacefully around 16:00.

location.summary: NOS identifies the Zwitsalterrein in Apeldoorn.

demands.summary: NOS says demonstrators had gathered to protest cabinet COVID measures and includes their view that the measures were disproportionate.

protester_violence.summary: NOS says the city demonstrations did not lead to disorder; no violence against state authorities is described for this assembly.

state_response.summary: NOS says attendees left peacefully; the reports do not describe an attempt to disperse this gathering. Four arrests elsewhere in Apeldoorn are not linked to attendees. No other response category is established.

notes: RTV Apeldoorn reported on 19 January that an announced demonstration organizer had canceled its planned event; NOS nevertheless directly reports about 400 people assembled at this location on 31 January. The identity or organizational link between the canceled plan and the actual gathering is unresolved, so no organizer is assigned. Four citywide arrests are not attributed to these attendees without direct evidence.
open_questions: Was this gathering associated with the organizer whose earlier announced demonstration was canceled?

title: Curfew-opposition gathering called at Nelson Mandela-plein in Breda
location: Nelson Mandela-plein and nearby intersections, Tuinzigt, Breda
organizer: An individual who posted a Facebook call; name not retained here
participants_original: Official court search excerpt: 40–50 people were in the area around 20:20. The opened retrospective report says about 70 people gathered that evening.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened retrospective report explicitly estimates about 70 people gathered in Tuinzigt in connection with the curfew-opposition call, above 50. The official court search excerpt gives 40–50 in the area around 20:20, leaving a time-specific discrepancy but not negating the report’s larger event-level estimate.

start_date.summary: The court excerpt and retrospective report place the curfew-opposition gathering on 24 January 2021.

location.summary: The sources identify Tuinzigt and the Nelson Mandela-plein area in Breda.

demands.summary: The call quoted by the retrospective report asked people opposed to the curfew to gather and said “Weg met de avondklok, weg met Rutte.”

organizer.summary: The court excerpt describes one individual posting a Facebook call; the person’s identity is not retained here.

participants_original.summary: A police account quoted in the search-only official court excerpt says 40–50 people were in the area at about 20:20; the opened retrospective report says about 70 people gathered that evening. The exact time/count basis is unresolved.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened retrospective report’s estimate of about 70 people gathered in connection with the curfew-opposition call exceeds 50; the official court snippet’s earlier 40–50 count is retained as a time-specific discrepancy.

protester_violence.summary: The report describes fires, barricades and private property damage after the gathering began, but does not document violence directed against the state by assembly participants. Leave unknown and do not attribute later acts to all attendees.

state_response.summary: The report describes an emergency order followed by riot-police intervention, supporting crowd_dispersal yes. It does not establish arrests, accommodation, beatings, killings or shootings directed at the assembly; those remain unknown.

end_date.summary: The report says calm returned after about fifteen minutes but does not establish when all participants physically left.

participants_estimate.summary: The opened report gives an approximate event-level estimate of about 70 people.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The report says an emergency order was issued and riot police intervened; this supports an attempt to break up the disorderly crowd, without establishing each attendee’s conduct.

notes: The opened retrospective report ties a roughly 70-person gathering to a social-media call against the curfew and against Rutte. An official court search excerpt gives a lower, time-specific count of 40–50 people in the area around 20:20; preserve this discrepancy. The report then describes fires, barricades and property damage as the atmosphere changed, and later an emergency order and ME intervention. Keep these later acts distinct from the policy protest and do not attribute them to every attendee.
open_questions: Can the official judgment body be accessed to verify its full police account and the time-specific crowd count?
Does the roughly 70 estimate refer to the exact same group and period as the 40–50 count?
When did all participants physically leave after the emergency order and ME intervention?
Were any arrests or force used against participants in the assembly itself?

title: Evening gathering at De Braak amid curfew-related disorder in Helmond
participants_original: The opened retrospective report says about 50 people, mostly young people from Helmond, gathered at De Braak that evening.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened retrospective report estimates about 50 people, which is near the threshold but does not provide a firm minimum; eligibility remains pending. The same report says the crowd was assembled amid signals about continuing riots, not that all were curfew protesters.

start_date.summary: The retrospective report places the De Braak gathering on Sunday 24 January 2021.

location.summary: The report identifies sportcomplex De Braak in Helmond.

participants_original.summary: The report estimates approximately 50 people, mostly young Helmond youths, gathered there that evening.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The approximate estimate is around the 50-person threshold; no precise minimum is stated.

protester_violence.summary: The report describes a gathering amid expected disorder but does not give a specific state-directed violent act by attendees at this assembly; leave unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The report says the riot police drove the group apart toward the city center and the situation quickly became calm.

end_date.summary: Police drove the group apart and the situation became calm, supporting a same-day end, though exact physical departure time is not given.

notes: This is an evening gathering at De Braak described in a retrospective report, distinct from X001, the announced afternoon curfew protest near the Helmond stadium where only a handful attended. The report says police and youth workers had signals that people wanted to continue riots; it estimates about 50 people gathered and says riot police drove the group apart. It does not establish that this crowd assembled to make a specific demand to the state, so it remains pending_state_target. The report says hooligans did not manifest during the COVID protests; do not convert this gathering into a COVID protest or assume all attendees took part in later disorder.
open_questions: Did the De Braak group itself state an opposition demand directed at Dutch state policy, or was it only expected to continue criminal disorder?
Does the approximate 50-person estimate establish at least 50 attendees?
Were any arrests or force directed at attendees beyond the riot-police dispersal?
